about: The day a term starts after its election where the office's own start rule is not carried on the office (federal offices carry theirs: January 20, January 3). A rule is data, never a fixed date: fixed (month, day); nth-weekday (month, weekday 0=Sunday, nth); weekday-after (the first weekday strictly after the anchor nth anchorWeekday of the month); weekday-after-day (the first weekday strictly after the month and day). Rows are keyed by state and then an office key (an office's own row wins) or office family. Read by src/core2/elections-calendar.ts termStartAfter. A state with no row for a family takes the default (SG-GOV-term-end-estimate). Legislator rows are listed only where the start differs from the executive's or is known; county and municipal terms come from their own calendars.

default.estimatedFrom: Most state and local terms begin in early January after the November election (state constitutions and charters); a state with no row here is not yet read.
